country: WHO European Region (50 of 53 Member States)

links.outcome: Member States offering AI training to the health workforce (in-service and pre-service)
links.effect: Only 24% (12/50) of Member States offered in-service AI training for the health workforce, and 20% (10/50) offered pre-service training.
links.quote: Finally, with regard to health workforce education and AI literacy, the study highlights a significant gap in preparedness, where only 24% of Member States (12/50) reported offering in-service AI training for the health workforce, and 20% (10/50) offered pre-service training.

links.outcome: Stakeholder groups engaged by Member States on AI, including patients and the public
links.effect: Of 36 Member States reporting engagement, patient associations were engaged by 42% (15/36) and the general public by 22% (8/36). Government actors (81%), providers (75%), and developers (75%) were engaged more often.
links.quote: Of the 36 Member States reporting at least one form of engagement, the stakeholders most frequently engaged were government actors (81%; 29/36), healthcare providers (75%; 27/36), and AI developers (75%; 27/36), whereas patient associations (42%; 15/36) and the general public (22%; 8/36) were less commonly involved.

screen.reason: Cross-sectional survey of 50 WHO European Region Member States on AI implementation, governance, workforce preparedness, and barriers across health systems.
